senses.gloss: m. (v. רַב II) [my teacher, my master,] Rabbi, title of scholars, esp. of the Tannaim, and of the Palestinian Amoraim.
units: B. Mets. 85ᵃ חכים … ור׳ קרו לך וכ׳ I shall make thee a ḥackim, and a gold-embroidered cloak they shall spread over thee, and Rabbi they shall call thee &c.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 84a:2-14">Ib. 84ᵃ</cite> <he>מאי … ר׳ קרו לי והכא ר׳ וכ׳</he> what good hast thou done me, there (among the Roman gladiators) they called me Rabbi (master), and here (as a scholar) they call me Rabbi.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 17b:9">Ab. Zar. 17ᵇ</cite> <he>ומ״ט קרו לך ר׳ רַבָּן וכ׳</he> and why do they call thee Rabbi? I am the chief master of weavers.
Ib. ר׳ אלעזר; a. v. fr.—Esp. Rabbi, surname of R. Judah han-Nasi.
<cite ref="Gittin 59a:18">Gitt. 59ᵃ</cite> <he>מימות משה ועד ר׳ וכ׳</he> from the days of Moses to those of Rabbi we do not meet with learning and high office in one place (combined in one person).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 85a:21">B. Mets. 85ᵃ</cite>; a. v. fr.
